title: Heat Transfer and Insulation
seo_title: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Heat Transfer and Insulation Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Heat transfer; insulation and energy saving; the national electricity supply system
standard_text: Heat is transferred by conduction, convection and radiation. Insulators reduce heat transfer and save energy. Electricity is generated in power stations and distributed through the national grid; energy is lost to the surroundings at every step, so we should save electricity. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 7, Energy and Change: Heat transfer; insulation and energy saving; the national electricity supply system)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): conduction, convection, radiation, conductors and insulators, saving energy and the national electricity grid. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation.
body_html:
How to think about it

Conduction moves heat through solids (a metal spoon in hot tea). Convection moves heat in liquids and gases as warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks. Radiation carries heat through empty space, such as from the Sun.

Insulators such as wool, polystyrene, air and ceiling insulation slow down heat transfer, keeping houses warm in winter and cool in summer. Electricity is made in power stations (mostly coal-fired), stepped up by transformers and carried through the national grid. Energy is wasted as heat at every step, so switching off and using solar geysers saves energy.

Example

Why does a metal spoon in hot soup become hot?

Through the solid

Answer: conduction

Example

Why is a heater placed low in a room?

Warm air rises.

Answer: convection currents spread the heat

Common mistakes

  • Thinking cold moves into things.
  • Thinking a blanket makes heat.
  • Thinking all electricity in South Africa comes from solar power.

faq.q: Why do houses with ceiling insulation use less electricity?
faq.a: Less heat escapes in winter and less enters in summer.

faq.q: Why is electricity sent at very high voltage?
faq.a: Less energy is lost as heat in the power lines.

items.q: A pan of water heats up from the bottom as hot water rises. Which type of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Conduction: through solids by particles vibrating. Convection: in liquids and gases as warm fluid rises. Radiation: infrared waves, even through a vacuum.

items.q: Lindiwe observes hot water rising and cold water sinking in a pot. Which kind of heat transfer is this mainly?

items.q: Why does a dark car get hotter in the sun than a white car?
c: Dark colours absorb more radiant energy.
items.e: Light colours reflect radiation.

items.q: Why are pot handles made of plastic or wood?

items.e: Insulators slow heat flow.

items.q: How does the Sun's heat reach Earth?

items.q: What is the difference between temperature and thermal energy?

items.e: A bath at 40 °C has more thermal energy than a cup at 90 °C.
